items.part: 2-cell AA holder, half-closed: bought ONLY for its spring/plate contacts, which are pulled out and pressed into the printed battery bay (2S series)
items.note: The holder body itself (about 57 x 31 x 15 mm) does NOT fit the 50 mm-cell belly. The CAD battery bay was lengthened to 53.6 mm inside (50.5 mm button-top cell + 2.3 mm compressed spring + 0.8 mm plate) and the cells raised 1.4 mm; cells clear the inner shell by 0.44 mm and the MG90S cases by 0.8 mm (src/build_rig.py prints the check). No 14500 cells with solder tabs and no ready 2S 14500 pack were found at Direnc or Robotistan on 2026-10-25, so tabbed cells are not an option. Never solder directly onto Li-ion cans.

The sleeve is a printed PETG bushing, Ø3.2 bore x Ø5.0 OD x 6.6 mm (hub bore Ø5.2), listed under print. It is included in the print price; a drop of light oil on assembly.

items.part: M3 nylon-insert lock nut (axles)
Neodymium magnet Ø6 x 1.5 mm (cap: 4 in cap + 4 in body)
items.note: No Ø6x2 mm was found in stock; the CAD and manifest now use Ø6x1.5 mm (pockets 1.5 mm deep, 0.4 mm skin). Holding force: an N35 Ø6x1.5 pair is roughly 3-4 N face to face, roughly 1.5-2 N through a 0.4 mm skin on each side, so 4 pairs give about 6-8 N against a cap of about 25 g (0.25 N): ample for handling, but a hard fall onto the cap can knock it off. That is acceptable, and arguably useful as a breakaway. Estimate from typical N35 data, not measured.

materials: PLA matte ivory/cream (e.g. Bambu Lab PLA Matte Ivory White or Elas PLA Krem, about #ECE3D0): lower body shell, hubs, ear inserts, toe-bean inserts, about 50 g

PLA matte caramel: Bambu Lab PLA Matte Caramel (A01-N3, catalogue swatch #AE835B) for the cap, ears, 4 arms+boots at 50 % gyroid and the hubcaps, about 65 g. Turkish availability NOT verified (not found at Robotistan or Direnc on 2026-10-25; ask the print studio). With a local light-brown/latte PLA instead, the tone will differ from the render
PLA any colour: inner chassis (servo cradles, lengthened 53.6 mm battery bay with contact slots, deck), about 10 g
PETG black: peanut visor + nose, printed outer face up; gloss only after sanding (400 -> 1500) + 2K clear coat, because ironing does not work on the curved visor, about 5 g
PETG any colour: 2 front-axle sleeves (Ø3.2 x Ø5.0 x 6.6 mm), under 1 g
Supports, brims and waste, about 10-15 g extra (tree supports only inside the 4 socket cups)
print.basis: Volumes from concept_C2/stl via trimesh: cream shell 23.4 cm3, caramel shell 22.1, legs (caramel) 40.5 solid (about 55 % effective at 50 % gyroid), hubs 11.4, visor/nose 2.7, tyres 5.7, chassis 11.7, giving about 110 g net (concept says about 112 g printed). Sliced with supports and brims, about 130-150 g. Time about 18-24 h on a Bambu-class printer (0.12 mm layers on the domes); 30 h or more on an older i3. Rates: there is no single public Turkish price list. A university tariff (OMÜ döner sermaye) lists PLA 5 TL/g, PETG 6 TL/g, TPU 7 TL/g (KDV incl.) with a 200 TL minimum, while hobby/Armut sellers quote 1.5-4 TL/g. Estimate: PLA 125 g x 3.5-5.5 = 440-690; PETG visor + axle sleeves 6 g plus a material-change/setup fee of 50-100 = 80-130; TPU tyres 8 g plus setup = 105-160; visor finish (sand + 2K clear) 0-150; one reprint for fit (magnet pockets, servo cradles, tyre stretch) 0-100. Total 650-1,200 TL; about 850 TL is typical. A resin visor is an option (+about 150 TL). This is 4 materials in separate jobs, not AMS multi-colour; all colour splits are separate parts.

shipping_basis: Free-shipping thresholds read on the shop pages: Robotistan, Direnc, Robo90 and Robolink 1,500 TL; Motorobit 2,500 TL (MNG/DHL); the Amazon item ships free. Below the threshold, about 90-150 TL per parcel is assumed; the shops do not publish the fee before checkout, so this is unverified. Up to 100 TL more is added for couriering the print if the studio is not local.

min_kit.part: Analog adjustable 60 W pen soldering iron

better_kit.part: ANENG SL105 60 W digital adjustable iron

tools.note: Tools cost 0 TL if the family already has a soldering iron and a multimeter. Buying the multimeter and iron at Direnc lifts that order over 1,500 TL and saves its shipping (about 90-150 TL).

total_basis: Minimum: required parts + 650 TL print + 4 paid parcels at 90 TL. Maximum: also the round-PCB GC9A01 swap (+387.80), a 1,200 TL print, 150 TL per parcel and 100 TL print courier. Typical: parts + 850 print + 480 shipping. Not included: optional lines (+400: hook-up wire and wall adapter, usually not needed) and tools (0 if owned, otherwise 434-1,041).

lean_variant.what: No on-robot audio (drop MAX98357A, INMP441 and speaker; voice goes through the phone app), no spare servo, reuse a USB-C cable from home. The Amazon order disappears. The Motorobit order is still needed (charger, BMS, DRV8833). Robotistan still clears 1,500 TL, so its shipping stays free.

changes_vs_concept: 2S charger: Robolink 78 TL replaced by Motorobit 181.80 TL. The Robolink page says 2 A charge, which is over the 14500's 900 mA max; the Motorobit module charges at 0.55 A from USB-C.
WS2812B moved from Robolink to Robo90 (4.76), and TTP223B moved from Robo90 to Direnc (14.53), to consolidate orders.
Magnets are Ø6x1.5 mm (Ø6x2 mm was not found in stock).

The concept's ~250 TL 'misc' line is replaced by itemised lines: switch, diodes, caps, resistors, perfboard, header, jumper ribbon, JST pigtails, heat-shrink, solder, screws, nuts, magnets, glue, USB cable.
All other prices are unchanged from the concept and were verified live on 2026-10-24. Small qty changes: MG90S 517, GC9A01 18, N20 26.

Battery: the 2xAA holder (Direnc 8.37) is now a source of spring/plate contacts for a printed bay. The CAD bay was lengthened from 50 to 53.6 mm and the cells were raised 1.4 mm (review fix: the holder itself is about 7 mm too long for the belly).
Front axles: M3x12 screw + printed PETG sleeve, so the wheel turns on a smooth sleeve (review fix: the concept's 'shoulder screw' is not in the BOM shops).
Caramel filament: Bambu Lab PLA Matte Caramel #AE835B, matching the manifest (the concept's Elas #CF8A46 is no longer used); the visor finish is sand + 2K clear, not ironing.
Magnets: Ø6x1.5 everywhere (manifest, CAD and BOM agree).
